subject: EU/APAC private deploy — residency & cross-region failover review
body:
From: Paul Moriarty <paul.moriarty@eurobank.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:14:00 +0000
Subject: Private deploy: EU/APAC residency & failover questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We’re compiling a short list of non-functional requirements for the formal procurement package and need a clear statement of how a Redwood Private deployment would satisfy:

- Data residency guarantees for EU customers (data at rest and metadata)
- Cross-border failover behavior: if EU region is unavailable, what happens to requests from EU customers? Can we ensure requests stay within a permitted jurisdiction?
- Network peering/topology recommendations for a dual-site (EU primary, APAC warm-standby) setup, including public IP requirements and VPN/Direct Connect equivalents
- Audit evidence we can hand to the InfoSec team (control plane logs, access logs, KMS key provenance)

Can you put together a short summary + any checklist items we should include? Also attaching our internal network slice request for reference.

Appreciate it —
Paul
IT Architecture, EuroBank

Attachment: eurobank-network-slice-request.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Paul Moriarty <paul.moriarty@eurobank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deploy: EU/APAC residency & failover questions

Paul — thanks for the clear list. I’m looping in Marissa (solutions) and Dylan (networking) so we can give a combined answer and provide artifacts. Below is an initial, high-level summary; we’ll follow with a short checklist PDF and a proposed mutual action plan.

High level answers (short):
- Data residency: For Private (VPC) deployments we support both customer-managed storage and Redwood-managed storage within the customer’s chosen region. For EU-only residency we recommend configuring all persistent volumes and object stores in the EU region and enabling KMS keys scoped to the EU key ring. Metadata (routing headers) can be configured to avoid leaving the EU control plane; see attachment for required config flags.
- Cross-border failover: By default, failover can be configured with a policy of "regional-only" (no cross-border promotion) or "controlled-failover" (promote warm-standby in APAC but only for non-sensitive customer profiles). We will not automatically route EU PII to APAC unless an explicit failover policy and legal signoff exist.
- Networking: Recommend site-to-site IPsec (or cloud provider private link) between EuroBank VPCs and the private deploy. Public IPs only required for admin/control-plane endpoints (can be restricted to a small allowlist). We'll provide an IP/port matrix and NAT recommendations.
- Evidence: We can produce a residency checklist, exported audit logs (S3/Blob with WORM retention), KMS key metadata (creation/rotation records), and a signed statement of where persistent data resides.

Next steps: Marissa will draft the checklist and provide the artifact set. Dylan will ingest the attached network slice and propose concrete CIDR/ASN/peer points.

I’ve attached a working checklist we use internally.

— Soojin
Principal, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-residency-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

Paul — attaching a concise artifact bundle for your InfoSec packet. Contents:
- residency_eu_apac_summary.txt — a plain-language summary of obligations and configurable controls
- redwood-residency-checklist.pdf — checklist of config steps and evidence exports
- demo-deploy-cfg.yaml — minimal example of region-scoped config flags

Checklist highlights (TL;DR):
1) Persistence: allocate EU-backed object storage + block volumes. Tag all volumes with customer_id and region.
2) KMS: create EU-scoped CMKs; Redwood will accept an external key policy or use a customer-provided HSM.
3) Control plane: deploy control plane endpoints into EuroBank's private subnet; restrict egress to your management CIDRs.
4) Logging: enable immutable export of control-plane and inference logs to your EU audit bucket with 10-year retention option.
5) Failover policy: set to REGIONAL_ONLY for any dataset marked as PII (default). For non-PII, set WARM_STANDBY with manual approval.

Delivery artifacts: I’ll upload these to the shared drive and provide a short checklist PDF suitable for procurement. Let me know if you prefer a one-page summary versus the full packet.

Cheers,
Marissa
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachment: residency_eu_apac_summary.txt (text/plain)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Moriarty <paul.moriarty@eurobank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 12:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deploy: EU/APAC residency & failover questions

Paul — quick network notes after a first pass on the attached slice request:

- Preferred topology: 2-site, active/warm with asymmetric routing. EU is active for all production prefixes. APAC sits idle for most prefixes with BGP session to advertise a smaller set of prefixes only during failover windows.
- BGP/Peering: We recommend establishing a BGP session between your on-prem edge and the Redwood private-hosted edge. We support MD5 auth and prefix filters; we will provide a sample policy.
- IP addressing: Keep unequal overlapping prefixes out — we’ll require explicit route maps for any shared ranges. Provide NAT64/translation plan if you need cross-jurisdiction API access for monitoring agents.
- Control-plane endpoints: Admin/control-plane must be allowed outbound to Redwood management IPs (list provided). We can also place the control-plane inside your VPC (no public IP) if you prefer fully private management.
- Testing: propose a table-top failover exercise: (1) simulate EU region loss, (2) run IP re-advertisement from APAC, (3) validate no EU-PIN code flows to APAC by inspecting headers. We’ll run the exercise in a staging window and capture packet-level traces.

I’ll prepare a concrete IP/port matrix and a short BGP playbook and share by EOD tomorrow. If EuroBank’s netops has preferred ASN/CIDR ranges, send over and I’ll slot them into the config.

– Dylan
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
